title: Declare each train participant once as wagon:, user: or system: id

facts.note: Needs an observer that classifies a planned artifact as a train workflow definition (legacy source: planner train convention). Any train definition that is authored, edited or reviewed falls in scope, whichever part of it changes.
Task text mentions authoring, changing or reviewing a train or its participants.

fires: Planner authors a new train and lists its participants
Planner adds a wagon, human role or external source to an existing train's participants
Planner edits any part of an existing train definition (e.g. its steps) whose participant declarations must still conform
Planner or reviewer checks a train's participant declarations
doesNotFire: Editing a wagon's own internal artifacts without touching or checking any train definition
Code-level changes that do not touch planning artifacts

given: A train workflow definition whose actors (wagons, human roles, external systems/data sources) are declared as participants
when: The planner authors, edits or checks that train's participant declarations
then: List each participant exactly once as `wagon:{wagon-id}`, `user:{role}` or `system:{source}`, matching `^(wagon|user|system):[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`.
prefer: Use `wagon:` for a wagon that performs processing, `user:` for a human actor's role, `system:` for an external system or data source
Make the id part start with a lowercase ASCII letter, followed by zero or more lowercase ASCII letters, digits or hyphens
avoid: Listing the same participant more than once
Using any type prefix other than wagon, user or system, or omitting the prefix
Uppercase letters, underscores, spaces or a leading digit or hyphen in the id part
Typing a human actor or an external source as a wagon (or the reverse)
why: Train steps move artifacts between declared participants, so a uniquely named, typed actor list keeps every step's source and destination unambiguous and checkable.
evidence: Every entry in the train's participants list matches `^(wagon|user|system):[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`
No participant string appears more than once in the list
Each participant's type matches its role: wagon = performs processing, user = human actor, system = external system/data source
verifier_detail: Term participant_type (label 'Participant types'): mapping type -> pattern. wagon -> wagon:{wagon-id} (performs processing); user -> user:{role} (human actor); system -> system:{source} (external system/data source)
Validation regex: ^(wagon|user|system):[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$ (consecutive or trailing hyphens in the id part are accepted by this regex)
Uniqueness: each participant listed once (exact string duplicates are findings)
